- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong upward momentum, model tends to overcorrect — dampen the final 3–5 forecast points.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 or negative values, model often underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% buffer to lower end of forecast range.  
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.7), model tends to overfit recent trends — smooth out forecast curve by reducing volatility in middle 10–15 days.  
- If forecast starts with a sharp drop after a recent spike, check sentiment history — if sentiment was neutral or negative, the drop may be premature; adjust upward by 3–5%.
